balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

ffoAdjPerShare.title: FFO as Adjusted per share
ffoAdjPerShare.content:
FFO as Adjusted is NAREIT FFO further adjusted for items the company deems non-comparable (debt extinguishment, impairments, promote income); dividing by shares gives the per-share house AFFO figure management guides to.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: this is the actual basis of the DCF's Owner FCF series (last_fcf), not the plain FFOPerShare column -- the two diverge because FFO as Adjusted nets out revenue- and non-revenue-enhancing capex and straight-line rent. The FY2026 dividend cut of ~45% tracks this series falling, not the headline FFO line.

What to watch:

  • Quarterly run-rate versus the annualized dividend after the cut
  • Gap between FFO as Adjusted and reported FFO widening (more capex/SL-rent adjustments)

sameStoreNoi.title: Same-store NOI growth
sameStoreNoi.content:
Same-store net operating income growth measures rental income less property operating expenses for the stabilized portfolio held in both periods, isolating organic performance from acquisitions and development lease-up. The cash basis excludes straight-line rent and fair-value lease adjustments.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: this turned negative through FY2026 (as low as -11.9% cash in Q1 2026) as life-science tenants gave back space -- the clearest read on the cyclical downturn, ahead of occupancy or revenue.

What to watch:

  • Cash growth trending more negative than GAAP growth (straight-line rent cushioning the headline number)
  • Sequential improvement signaling the trough has passed

rentalRateChange.title: Rental rate change (leasing spreads)
rentalRateChange.content:
Rental rate change compares the starting rent on new and renewal leases against the expiring rent on the same space, on a GAAP (straight-line) and cash basis.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: spreads were strongly positive through FY2023-FY2024 (GAAP +29.4%, +16.9%) when life-science demand was tight, then went negative in 2026 (as low as -15.8% cash in Q1) -- tenants are now re-leasing at lower rents than before, the leasing-market mirror of the same-store NOI decline.

What to watch:

  • Cash spreads turning positive again as the first sign of a leasing recovery
  • Volume of space re-leased (see leasing RSF KPIs) alongside the rate, not rate alone

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

occupancy.title: Occupancy
occupancy.content:
The share of lettable space (or units) that is leased.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: occupancy below the sector norm is the first sign of rental pressure.

What to watch:

  • Occupancy trend
  • Lease expiries in the next two years

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
